thread:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD-6789. Rule: inference-gateway-5xx-rate. 5m window: 18% 5xx (502/504), spike focused in eu-west1. Top route: /v1/generate. Logs: https://logs.redwood.example/r/PD-6789

jess (on-call): Acked. I'm on it, looking at gateway and auth-proxy traces.

jess (on-call): Quick check — upstreams show repeated `upstream reset` and `502` from auth-proxy cluster. Grabbing pod logs now.

raj (eng-infra): @jess can you paste a sample trace-id? I want to see if this aligns with the KV-cache eviction pattern from last week.

jess (on-call): trace: 0a1b2c3d4e. Log snippet:
```
[2026-02-18T02:45:12Z] request_id=0a1b2c3d4e method=POST path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=auth-proxy-12 reason="upstream reset"
[2026-02-18T02:45:12Z] auth-proxy-12 stderr: runtime: failed to allocate kv-cache segment
```

mike (ops): Noted customer-facing route. CS pinged. Sam, any customer reports?

sam (cs): Yep — two enterprise accounts reported failures ~02:44Z. They see 502 on product calls. I told them we're investigating and will update in 15m.

jess (on-call): Trying runbook step 2: reduce route weight to eu-west1 by 80% and shift to eu-central1. Running control-plane command now.

mike (ops): Initiating weight shift via orchestration: 
```bash
redwood-routectl set-weight --route /v1/generate --region eu-west1 --weight 20
redwood-routectl set-weight --route /v1/generate --region eu-central1 --weight 80
```

incidentbot: PD-6789 escalated: no auto-resolve after 10m -> paging L2.

raj (eng-infra): If auth-proxy is OOMing on kv allocations, quick mitigation is to warm cache and restart the smallest subset. Can we restart one pod at a time?

jess (on-call): Doing rolling restart on auth-proxy-12..15 (one at a time) as per runbook. Warming KV cache post-restart.

mike (ops): Started restart sequence. First pod restarted and healthy. Metrics: 5xx dropped from 18% -> 6% after weight shift + restart. Observability: https://metrics.redwood.example/d/PD-6789

sam (cs): Customers updated: "errors subsided, looks better". I told them we'll keep them posted.

jess (on-call): Monitoring for 15m. If stable, we'll keep reduced weight and schedule a deeper postmortem. Leaving notes in PD ticket.

mike (ops): +1 on postmortem. Any suspected root cause? Raj?

raj (eng-infra): Early guess: kv-cache allocator regression combined with a recent auth-proxy config tweak increased memory churn under certain request patterns. Need to repro in staging.

incidentbot: PD-6789: acked by jess (on-call), escalated to raj (eng-infra) for follow-up.

jess (on-call): Handing off to @raj for night rotation in 30m. Key items in handoff: weight shift in place, restarted auth-proxy subset, customers notified, temporary mitigation active.

raj (eng-infra): Taking over. I'll keep the reduced weight until we validate a fix. Creating follow-up ticket: INF-4098 and linking PD-6789. Leaving details: logs, snippets, runbook steps taken.

sam (cs): Thanks — will send final update to affected customers and mark as "monitoring".

jess (on-call): :thumbsup: handing off now.

raj (eng-infra): Confirmed — last check: 5xx ~2.9% over 5m. I'll post findings and rollback plan if it recurs.

incidentbot: PD-6789 status -> monitoring. Auto-close disabled until ENG confirms root cause.
